### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**10** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **68** of **251** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **176** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 65ee4b7ad49361bc3cfaf3a32c9ed02752d4a152` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ff3d5ce74645f6c59abf7a09935788ebebd3f896` — the merge of head `15e41882289f6745017657fda3e975fccecf8e13` into base `65ee4b7ad49361bc3cfaf3a32c9ed02752d4a152`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ff3d5ce74645f6c59abf7a09935788ebebd3f896 && git checkout ff3d5ce74645f6c59abf7a09935788ebebd3f896
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 65ee4b7ad49361bc3cfaf3a32c9ed02752d4a152 15e41882289f6745017657fda3e975fccecf8e13 && git checkout -B drift-repro 65ee4b7ad49361bc3cfaf3a32c9ed02752d4a152 && git merge --no-ff 15e41882289f6745017657fda3e975fccecf8e13

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 65ee4b7ad49361bc3cfaf3a32c9ed02752d4a152
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `15e41882289f6745017657fda3e975fccecf8e13`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-translated-echo.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-discovery-and-bases.ts

Read for this record: card #36595 (body and its three comments: triage 7089293793, claim 7118543153, dev report 7119401800), PR #36813 (body, both comments, the five-file net diff against `main`), and the 73 check-runs on the head. `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-translated-echo.test.ts` was read for agreement with the two implementing files; the changeset and the test are the lane seat's ACCEPT. Code outside the diff was read, not reviewed: `registry-platform-global.ts` (`getPackagedObjectBase`, `getPackagedObjectOwner`, `packagedPlacedRelatedLists`), `registry-object-registration.ts` (the `overlay ?? own` fold), `registry-extension-placement.ts` (`arrangementDeclared`), `translateObjectRelatedLists` in the resolver, and the call site in `protocol-save.ts`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Published accept set: unchanged — right.** No schema, no `.describe()`, no exported symbol moves. The `packages/spec` change is one TSDoc block on `TranslateDocumentOptions.packagedBase`; it ships in the `.d.ts`, so it is a published sentence and is judged for truth in ④.
- **Public surface of `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`: unchanged — right.** `restoreTranslatedEchoes` gains an optional `packagedOwner` argument and the facet method's `host` pick gains `engine`; neither the module nor the facet is exported from the package index, and the only callers are `protocol-discovery-and-bases.ts` and `protocol-save.ts`. The two callers that pass no owner (`source: item` in the stored-row migration, `source: undefined` in the pure injected-column half) get an empty extender cut and behave as on `main`.
- **Save-door behaviour: one stored value changes, nothing is refused — right as declared.** A `PUT /meta/object/NAME` body whose field label, option label or `relatedLists` entry label (a) sits on a field or `list` the stored row does not declare at all, (b) is brought by an enabled code extender (not declared or named by the packaged owner), and (c) equals what the translator makes of the extender's packaged text in some locale, is now stored as that packaged text and named on `advisories` (`translated-label-echo`). Every body the door accepted is still accepted with the same status.
- **Gate verdicts.** All 73 check-runs on the head are `success` or `skipped` (Test Core 10/10 shards, Build Core, the type-check lanes, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Spec property liveness`, the lint lanes). The four gates the dev report lists as not measured locally (`check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test`, `check:dts-closure`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure`) are answered by the green lint and build lanes on this head. The dogfood matrix is skipped, which is what a PR with no `!` and no `(narrowing)` arm owes.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/metadata-protocol: patch` and `@objectstack/spec: patch` match the diff: a bug fix in a released package, and a doc comment that ships in the declaration file. `Check Changeset` is green on the head.
- `Clause-②: no` holds. The question asked of this PR was whether the door now refuses or alters something a client could send before. It refuses nothing. It alters one case: the translation of an extender's text, on a slot the stored row does not carry, is stored as the source text. That is the restore rule the door already applies to every other translated slot, reaching one more source. The earlier extensions of the same restore (the field `relatedListTitle` slot, the patch-entry source of #34784, the `relatedLists` entry label of #36574) shipped without the `(narrowing)` arm; the arm on #29790 was carried by its `422` refusal. An author who deliberately types exactly the translation gets the source stored, and the reader in that locale is served the same text from the catalog, as the module header already states for every other source. No capability is taken away at the consumer.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` holds: no key, value or requirement an author can write is added, refused or given a new default.
- `Refs #36595 (items 1, 2, 3)` is the partial-landing spelling; no closing keyword stands next to the card number, so the card stays open for item 4.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev flag — item 1 reachability measured by reading, not reproduced over HTTP.** Answered: the chain holds in the tree. `GET /meta/object/NAME` translates the folded object against `getPackagedObjectBase` (`packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts`), the fold starts from `overlay ?? own` and splices placements onto a base that declares a non-empty `relatedLists`, and `saveMetaItemUnaudited` calls `restoreTranslatedObjectEchoes` after every refusal and before the put. The door test in the diff pins the hand-over; the ablation in the dev report (owner hand-over removed: 1 failed) shows the test reads it.
- **Dev flag — four local gates not measured.** Answered by the head's check-runs (①).
- **Dev flag — the two same-named `packagedOwner` identifiers.** Answered: `args.packagedOwner` (the owner's declaration) is read only outside `sourceOf`; inside it the callback parameter of the same name is the patch-entry slot owner. No shadowed read; the names read alike and nothing more.
- **`open_questions` — item 4 (tighten `translation-target-unknown`, option A a `(narrowing)` card, option B document the bound).** Escalated to the seat. At read time the card carries no answer to it (three comments: triage, claim, dev report). Nothing in this diff touches `packages/lint`, and no sentence of the changed docblock, the module header or the door docblock describes or promises the lint behaviour, so leaving it out makes nothing here false.
- **Item 2 (N4), the "seat-accepted deviation" the PR body cites (2026-11-24T01:45Z).** Escalated to the seat for the record only: that acceptance is not on the card or the PR thread at read time. On the merits the card left "fix or documented deviation" open, the deviation serves no wrong text, and ④ finds the sentence that documents it true.
- **SQL push-down.** Not engaged: the diff adds one in-memory registry lookup (`getPackagedObjectOwner`, a `Map` find) and no query, id materialisation or in-app join.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts` — the `packagedBase` docblock, sentence by sentence against the head.**

- "where the owner declares `relatedLists`, those `relatedLists` carry each entry a code extender's list placement (`place`) splices in, as the fold splices it" — true. `SchemaRegistry.getPackagedObjectBase` replaces the owner's `relatedLists` with the output of `applyExtensionPlacements` run over the owner's own declaration, with the fold's own disabled-package filter and child-ownership test, and returns the owner unchanged where no placement applies.
- "so a placed tab's `label` reads the catalog" — true. `translateObjectRelatedLists` judges a served entry against the base entry of the same `list`; a served placed label equal to the base's reads the unchanged catalog.
- "Its scalars and every field the owner declares stay the owner's ... a patched owner field still reads as diverged" — unchanged text, still true: the base spreads `owner.definition` and widens only `validations`, added field names and the placed lists.
- "Whether a placement applies is judged on the OWNER here and on the served object's base layer (a tenant overlay's own `relatedLists`, else the owner's) by the fold" — true. The base calls `applyExtensionPlacements(owner, ...)`; the fold calls it on `merged`, which starts from `overlay ?? own`, and an extension body's `relatedLists` is not merged in before that pass.
- "where only a tenant overlay declares `relatedLists`, the served placed tab has no packaged counterpart, so it reads as authored and the deployment catalog does not translate its `label`" — true. The base then carries no `relatedLists`, the translator's `packagedEntries` is empty, the entry counts as diverged and reads `catalogs.changed`, never the deployment catalog. This is card item 2 stated as it behaves, not a promise of a fix.
- The docblock says nothing about `translation-target-unknown` or any lint verdict: item 4 is not promised.

**`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-translated-echo.ts` — the extender source against its header and the docblock.**

- The cut agrees with the contract. Fields: an incoming name the packaged base carries, the owner does not declare and the stored row does not declare. Lists: a base object-form entry whose `list` neither the owner nor the stored row names, bare or object form. It is asked last, so the stored row, the patch entries and the injected columns keep their precedence.
- The defence holds for the edge. With a stored row that declares `relatedLists` without the placed entry, the stored source answers `NOT_DECLARED`, the extender source carries the packaged entry, its reads are translated with the read's own options, and the body's translation is put back to the packaged label. The same path restores an added field's text slots and option labels.
- It does not break a legitimate save, tried four ways. (1) A title or label the stored row declares is excluded from the cut by name, so a tenant rename is the stored row's to explain, even when it equals a catalog string (pinned by the test). (2) An owner's field or entry the stored row dropped is excluded by the owner sets; the header's claim that the fold does not serve it is true, since the fold's base is the overlay body whole. (3) With no stored row the door's source is the packaged base itself, so the stored sets cover every extender name and the cut is empty. (4) A Studio or repository-editor save sends the stored document, so its entries are stored-declared or absent; an author who newly adds the placed entry with a label of their own keeps it unless it equals a translation of the packaged label, the header's standing edge, where the reader in that locale is served the same text.
- The extender source cannot explain an object scalar (the cut carries none), and a stored bare-string entry of the placed list blocks the cut, which matches the fold: a list the base already arranges keeps its entry and gains no label.
- A disabled extender adds nothing to the packaged base, so it adds nothing to the cut; a registry without `getPackagedObjectBase` returns the owner by reference and the identity guard leaves the cut empty.

**`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-discovery-and-bases.ts` — the door.**

- The owner is read from the same registry the base comes from, only when a base exists, and handed over only when defined. The docblock paragraph added above the method says what the code does. The read sits outside a `try`; it is a contributor-map lookup with no store behind it, so the door's "a degraded MetadataService fails nothing here" sentence stays true.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

- N1 — "declares `relatedLists`" in the docblock (and "a stored row of any age" in the module header) is looser than the code: both the base and the fold place a list only where the layer they judge declares a NON-EMPTY `relatedLists` (`arrangementDeclared`). An owner or stored row with `relatedLists: []` gets no placed entry on either side. No slot is served or stored differently from what the sentences lead a reader to expect in the non-empty case; left as an accepted deviation or a follow-up, since a fix moves the head.
- N2 — in the docblock's first paragraph the new placement clause is joined to the aside that follows the dash ("... what its extender ships, and, where the owner declares ..."), so the third thing the base carries reads as part of the reason for the second. Meaning is recoverable and true; wording only.

**VERDICT: PASS**

### Checklist
- **Shape:** `l1-face` CLEAN. Draft, base `main`, first line `Refs #36595 (items 1, 2, 3; item 4 is left out and reported to the seat as a fork)`. That is the partial-landing spelling `execution-duties.md` prescribes (`Refs #N (item k)`, never `Fixes`). No closing keyword binds any card, so the card stays open for item 4.
- **Checks at this head:** 73 check-runs. 60 success, 13 expected skip, 0 failed. Lint & Repo Gates and TypeScript Type Check: success. `mergeable_state` clean.
- **Governance:** `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 36813`: NOT governed, 236 lines.
- **Declarations:** `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` in the body and the changeset; they match the claim. The contract review's ② agrees: the save door refuses nothing new. It stores an extender's translation as source text on a slot the stored row does not declare, which is the existing restore rule reaching one more source. Precedents #34784 and #36574 shipped the same way without a narrowing arm.
- **Changeset:** `@objectstack/metadata-protocol: patch` and `@objectstack/spec: patch`. Both are published, and both have `src/**` moved; spec's is the `packagedBase` TSDoc in `i18n-resolver.ts`, which ships. The prose, read sentence by sentence:
  - the translated `/meta` read of a placed tab or added field over a stored row that predates the package: true;
  - the save door compares with the packaged definition as a last resort, only for a slot the stored row does not declare: true;
  - the slot is named in `advisories` (`translated-label-echo`): true;
  - a tenant's rename is never compared with the package: true;
  - an owner entry the stored row dropped is left as sent: true;
  - Console and Studio save the stored document, so they never reached this: consistent with the PR's reachability reading;
  - the `packagedBase` note on judging placement on the owning package vs the served object: matches `getPackagedObjectBase` and the `overlay ?? own` fold, per the contract review.

  Each sentence is pinned by a case in `protocol-translated-echo.test.ts`.
- **Scope:** five files, inside the claim's surface: `protocol-translated-echo.ts`, `protocol-discovery-and-bases.ts`, the `i18n-resolver.ts` docblock, tests and a changeset. The lint file named for item 4 is untouched, as intended.
- **Item 1 acceptance (the card's Re-check):** "a test pins that a non-source-locale save of a placed title, with a stored row lacking the entry, keeps the source title". It is pinned twice: in the restore unit (`'Audit trail'`, `'Market'`, restored paths), and through the save door handing over the packaged owner (`relatedLists[acme_audit].label`, `fields.cb_market.label`). A positive control shows the read really translates (`审计`, `市场`).
- **Ablations** (report 7119401800): extender source removed, 3 red; door hand-over removed, 1 red.
- **Item 2:** shipped as a documented deviation in the `packagedBase` docblock. The contract review reads every sentence of it as true.
- **Item 3:** done.
- **UI strings:** none.

### Findings
Must-fix: none. Should-fix: none. The contract review's N1 ("declares `relatedLists`" is looser than the code's non-empty test) and N2 (clause placement in the docblock's first paragraph) are wording nits with no slot served or stored wrongly. They are accepted as they stand.

### Before landing (paper, seat; not a finding on this diff)
The contract review's ③ found two seat routes the PR body relies on that are not on GitHub. Card #36595 carries only triage, the claim and the dev report.
- the "seat-accepted deviation" for item 2 that the PR body cites;
- the route of item 4 (the dev's `open_questions`: a `(narrowing)` card vs documenting the bound; per the area thread it goes to a later Tier H PR on this card).

Post both on #36595 before or with the partial `Release:` after merge, so the card records why item 2 shipped as documented and where item 4 goes.

### Landing notes
`Refs`: the card stays open and keeps its claim until item 4's route is executed; the area's partial Release follows the merge.
